summary: Tiered failsafe for prefetch+quant profile unwind causing tail latency for dedicated tenant
description:
Issue summary: After applying a tenant-scoped optimizer profile that enabled aggressive KV prefetch, async batching and a 4-bit quantization profile, BrightHealth AI reported an increase in tail latency (p95/p99) and occasional stalled streams for production inference. Impact: Customer-facing latency regressions for critical workflow (clinical-summarization), increased error rate for streaming sessions, and elevated token cost due to retries. This tenant is on a dedicated capacity pool with pinned redwood-open-7b-v2.

Recent changes: Tenant opt-profile v2.7 pushed at 2026-03-09 02:12 UTC enabling kv_prefetch=true, async_batcher.size=64, quant_profile=dynamic-4bit. Initial rollout was 100% for the tenant via traffic-gate. First symptoms were observed ~30m after rollout.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use dedicated tenant environment for BrightHealth AI (prod:us-east).
2) Apply optimizer profile: kv_prefetch=true, async_batcher.size=64, quant_profile=dynamic-4bit, batching.window_ms=20.
3) Replay the baseline prompt set (clinical-summarization-fast) at steady QPS (10 rps) with production seq lengths (avg 600 tokens).
4) Observe p95/p99 latency and streaming connection stability over 10-minute window.
logs: Serving logs (sample): 2026-03-09T02:46:10Z ERROR stream: write failed: timeout; request_id=tx-7f6c22
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Aggressive kv_prefetch combined with 4-bit quantization increases memory pressure and leads to intermittent stall when KV cache eviction coincides with async batching flushes.

Hypothesis B: Quantization kernel path for dynamic-4bit on this GPU type (A10G) has a regression when sequence length >> typical (we see avg 600 tokens) causing occasional long token times for affected batches.
SRE checks: node-level GPU memory clumps noted on nodes serving this tenant around spike times; no cluster-wide OOMs. Autoscaler not triggered due to dedicated capacity hard limits.
Telemetry: tail events correlate with bursts of long-sequence requests and with async_batcher.size reaching 64 (batches consolidating heterogeneous seq lengths).
temporary_workaround: Applied staged traffic-split at 2026-03-10T05:00 UTC: 80% traffic to primary tenant pool with optimizer.safemode=true (auto-reduce prefetch and async batching), 20% to fallback model variant (redwood-open-7b-v2-int8-fallback). Observed p95 reduced by ~35% within 6 minutes.
planned_actions: 1) Create and run a granular rollback script to atomically toggle tenant optimizer flags in the control plane (commands prepared and tested in staging).

2) Stepwise unwind sequence: disable kv_prefetch -> reduce async_batcher.size from 64 to 16 -> set quant_profile to int8-fallback. Each step will be gated with a 5-minute observation window and baked telemetry checks.
3) If unwind does not restore SLOs, execute controlled traffic migration to customer-dedicated fallback pool with int8 models and raise a support incident for capacity expansion options.
4) Postmortem: capture optimizer runbook updates and add automated canary that monitors kv_prefetch_evictions and async_batch_drop_rate for future rollouts.
resolution_notes: Partial mitigation applied (traffic split + optimizer.safemode). Full staged unwind playbook prepared and validated in staging. No code changes required; changes are control-plane config toggles. Customer has been informed and a short maintenance window (10 minutes per step) was agreed for the binary unwind. Follow-up: complete staged unwind on 2026-03-13 and monitor for 24 hours before closing ticket.
